text: Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed, randomly connected hidden layer called the "reservoir," which processes input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically fixed and not trained, making the training process simpler. Only the output weights are adjusted to fit the specific task, such as anomaly detection. Reservoirs in ESNs are often trained using random connectivity patterns to ensure a rich, diverse set of activations that can capture complex temporal dynamics.
